changes.before: economic activity has been rising moderately so far this year
changes.after: economic activity has been rising at a solid rate despite hurricane-related disruptions

changes.before: Job gains have remained solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.
changes.after: Although the hurricanes caused a drop in payroll employment in September, the unemployment rate declined further.
Gasoline prices rose in the aftermath of the hurricanes, boosting overall inflation in September; however, inflation for items other than food and energy remained soft.

changes.before: Higher prices for gasoline and some other items in the aftermath of the hurricanes will likely boost inflation temporarily; apart from that effect, inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term
changes.after: Inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term

changes.before: In October, the Committee will initiate the balance sheet normalization program described in the June 2017 Addendum to the Committee's Policy Normalization Principles and Plans.
changes.after: The balance sheet normalization program initiated in October 2017 is proceeding.

parsed.rationale: The upgrade of activity to 'solid rate' and the unemployment rate having 'declined further' strengthen the case for continued gradual hikes, only partly offset by the note that core inflation 'remained soft'. Policy guidance and the rate decision are unchanged, so the shift is modestly hawkish.

spans.quote: economic activity has been rising moderately so far this year
Job gains have remained solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.

Higher prices for gasoline and some other items in the aftermath of the hurricanes will likely boost inflation temporarily; apart from that effect, inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term
In October, the Committee will initiate the balance sheet normalization program described in the June 2017 Addendum to the Committee's Policy Normalization Principles and Plans.
